preconditions.expression: all(c.isalpha() or c.isdigit() for c in input_string)
preconditions.description: The input string contains only alphabetic characters (a-z) and numeric digits (0-9).

preconditions.expression: all(len(num) == 1 or (len(num) == 2 and num[0] == '2' and num[1] in '0123456') for num in re.findall(r'\d+', input_string))
preconditions.description: Any numeric sequence in the input is either a single digit or a two-digit number starting with '2' (i.e., 20-26).
No numeric sequence in the input has three or more digits.

postconditions.expression: all((c.isalpha() and (c in alphabetnums or c.lower() in alphabetnums)) or (c.isdigit() and (int(c) <= 26 or (len(c) == 2 and int(c) <= 26))) for c in output_string)
postconditions.description: Every character in the output string is either a valid letter (a-z) or a valid numeric representation (1-26, including '26').

postconditions.expression: all((c.isalpha() and (output_string[i] == str(alphabet.index(c.lower()) + 1) if c.islower() else str(alphabet.index(c.upper()) + 1))) or (c.isdigit() and (int(c) <= 26 and output_string[i] == alphabet[int(c) - 1])) for i, c in enumerate(input_string))
postconditions.description: For each alphabetic character in the input, the output contains its numeric equivalent (1-26), and for each numeric character in the input, the output contains its corresponding letter (a-z).
The output string has the same length as the input string.
